title: Satyricon: De Nuptiis Philologiae et Mercurii
shelf_note: Grotius's 1599 Raphelengius edition of Martianus Capella, the late-antique Neoplatonic allegory of the liberal arts. It belongs on an early-European-books shelf and next to Hermetic/Neoplatonic material.
structure_note: The printed page numbers are consistent with the scan index (scan 115 = p. 80, 231 = p. 196, 347 = p. 312, a constant offset of 35). 458/464 pages have OCR and 452 are translated. Nothing looks broken.

title: De Trinitatis Erroribus: Michael Servetus (PH474)
shelf_note: A 17th-century manuscript copy of Servetus's anti-Trinitarian treatise from the BPH. It belongs with heterodox and spiritualist theology.
structure_note: The photographs are open-book spreads, not split: page 42 carries a strip of the facing leaf, and page 122 carries half of it. The scan index runs 4–6 ahead of the manuscript pagination (42 = p. 38, 82 = p. 76, 122 = p. 116). The OCR's page-num for 82 says 56, which is a misread. 162 pages, all OCR'd, 160 translated.

book_verdict: The photographs are unsplit spreads. The OCR reads the facing leaf as a second column (p. 42) or interleaves both leaves line by line (p. 122), and the translation turns the mix into confident prose with invented completions. A Servetus specialist would reject two of these three pages on sight.

title: Sermons against the Turks
shelf_note: A late-15th-century humanist manuscript oration urging Pope Sixtus IV ('beatissime pater', 'dominum meum Sixtum') to crusade against the Turks. It has no tradition or collection set; as a primary source it fits a general Latin shelf. 'Sermons' is loose: it reads as one address to the pope.
structure_note: 34 pages, all OCR'd but only 19 translated, so roughly half the book has no English. There are no printed page numbers to check.

book_verdict: A heavily abbreviated Gothic cursive hand. The OCR is a good-faith reading but repeatedly misexpands nomina sacra and abbreviations (christianorum → proximorum/canis/caritate, pro fidei → perfidie). The translation papers over every misreading in fluent English, including one reversed clause. Readable for the gist; not quotable without the image.

title: Horoscopion generale dignoscendis horis cuiuscumque generis aptissimum …
shelf_note: Petrus Apian's 1533 Ingolstadt treatise on a universal time-and-mensuration instrument: early modern science and astronomy. The 'americana' collection tag reflects the John Carter Brown holding, not the content.
structure_note: 48 pages, all OCR'd, 43 translated. The signatures follow in order (B on 13, C 2 on 23). Nothing stands out.

ocr_errors.problem: 'in this age of ours' is read as 'in this little bundle', and the translation renders it as 'in this manual of ours'
silent normalisation of ampersands, ligatures and abbreviations (et, ae), done consistently

tr_errors.source: Quamvis in hoc nostro fasciculo a plerisque … videmus
tr_errors.english: Although in this manual of ours we see the hours of the Jews being used by many
tr_errors.problem: follows the misread. Apian complains about common usage 'in our age', not 'in this manual'

ocr_errors.problem: one hour/minute cell is wrong in the Markab table. All other cells checked in the four tables match the print (printer's errors such as '1127' and '0587' are reproduced or silently fixed)
letter slip
catchword dropped

tr_errors.english: Multiply 100 by 10, and 1000 will result
tr_errors.problem: the printer's error (100) is silently corrected to 1000 without a note. The correction is right, but the text no longer shows what the page prints

book_verdict: A good book: accurate OCR of the prose and of four dense star-time tables (one wrong cell found), and faithful translation. The only meaning slip is 'fasciculo' for 'saeculo'.

title: Opuscoli di Leonardo Pisano
shelf_note: Boncompagni's 1856 edition of Fibonacci's minor works (Flos, Liber quadratorum, Epistola): medieval Latin mathematics with Italian editorial notes. It fits early-science material. The 'americana' tag is an IA collection artefact.
structure_note: Scan index vs printed page: 42 = p. 7, 84 = p. 51, 125 = p. 96. That is 42 scans for 44 printed pages, then 41 scans for 45 printed pages, so about 6 printed pages are missing between the sampled leaves. They could be missing leaves in the Google scan, or plates paginated without scans; it should be checked. 167 pages, all OCR'd, 148 translated.

book_verdict: Clean modern print, mostly accurate OCR. But the algebra page flattens every fraction to 2/7, which breaks Fibonacci's worked solution in both panes, and the Liber quadratorum page's translation runs past the page break into text that is not there. The scan may also be missing a few leaves.
